items.title: 10.2 Graphical Solution of Trigonometric Equation (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 278-281: 10.2 Graphical Solution of Trigonometric Equation, intro, Examples 4-8, Figures 10.1-10.5, Note box

blocks.text: Pichle sabaq (10.1) mein humne trigonometric equations ko identities aur quadrants ki madad se algebra ke zariye hal kiya tha. Lekin har equation itni meharbaan nahin hoti. Aaj hum ek naya hathiyar seekhenge: graph. Idea bilkul seedha hai: equation ke dono sides ko alag alag graph bana kar ek hi paper par draw karo, aur jahan yeh dono graphs ek doosre ko kaatte (intersect karte) hain, wahi equation ke solutions hain.

Kitab kehti hai: jab equation \(f(x) = g(x)\) ki shakal mein ho, to aksar exact (bilkul theek) solution nikalna mushkil hota hai. Kuch equations identities aur properties se algebraically hal ho jati hain, magar bohat si itni complex hoti hain ke yeh tareeqe kaam nahin karte. Aisi soorat mein graphical method ek qeemti mutabadil (alternative) hai. Hum \(y = f(x)\) aur \(y = g(x)\) dono ko coordinate plane par plot karte hain aur aankh se dekhte hain ke woh kahan milte hain. In intersection points ke \(x\)-coordinates hi woh solutions hain jo \(f(x) = g(x)\) ko satisfy karte hain. Is tareeqe se humein yeh bhi pata chal jata hai ke total kitne solutions hain, aur yeh bhi samajh aata hai ke dono functions kaise behave karte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Graph ki zaroorat kyun parti hai? Equation \(\sin x = \frac{x}{2}\) ko dekhiye. Ek taraf \(x\) sine ke andar band hai, doosri taraf \(x\) bahar khula para hai. Koi bhi identity aisi nahin jo \(x\) ko dono jagah se nikaal kar ek taraf akela kar de. Aisi equations ko transcendental equations (woh equations jo sirf algebra se hal nahin hotin) kehte hain.
Yeh tareeqa sahi kyun hai? Agar koi point \((a, b)\) dono graphs par hai, to \(b = f(a)\) bhi hai aur \(b = g(a)\) bhi. Yani \(f(a) = g(a)\): \(a\) equation ka root hai. Ulta bhi sach hai: har root par dono graphs ek hi height par hote hain, yani wahan milte hain.
Ek misaal se sochiye: do dost ek hi sarak par chal rahe hain, ek seedha (line) aur doosra lehraata hua (wave). Jahan dono ek hi jagah aur ek hi waqt par hon, wohi "milne ke points" hain. Hum bas yeh points dhoondte hain.
Tareeqa, qadam ba qadam:
1. Equation ko \(f(x) = g(x)\) ki shakal mein likhiye; har side ek graph banegi.
2. Interval tay kijiye (sawal mein diya ho, ya trigonometric side ki range se nikaaliye).
3. Dono functions ki values ki chhoti si table banaiye, maslan \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke multiples par.
4. Dono graphs ek hi axes par, ek hi scale par draw kijiye.
5. Intersection points gin kar un ke \(x\)-coordinates parhiye.
6. Har value ko dono sides mein rakh kar check kijiye.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(x\) hamesha radians mein hota hai. Wajah yeh ke \(x\) trigonometric function ke bahar bhi aa raha hai; \(\frac{x}{2}\) ek aam number hai, aur use \(\sin x\) ke saath tabhi compare kar sakte hain jab angle bhi real number ho, yani radians. Degrees mein \(x = 90\) rakhein to \(\frac{x}{2} = 45\) ho jayega, jo bilkul bemaani hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Graph paper par amli tareeqa (exam mein bohat kaam aata hai):
1. Pehle \(x\)-axis par scale tay kijiye. \(\pi\) ko \(3.14\) maan kar marks lagaiye; maslan agar 2 cm = 1 unit ho to \(\pi\) taqreeban 6.3 cm par aayega aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) taqreeban 3.1 cm par.
2. \(y\)-axis ka scale is tarah rakhiye ke dono graphs ki sab se oonchi aur sab se neechi values page par aa jayen.
3. Table ke points halki pencil se lagaiye. Sine aur cosine ki lehar ko haath se smooth (hamwar) curve ki tarah milaiye, nok daar kone na banaiye.
4. Seedhi line ruler se kheenchiye; us ke liye do points kaafi hain, teesra point sirf tasdeeq ke liye.
5. Har crossing par ek chhota dot lagaiye aur wahan se \(x\)-axis tak dotted line giraiye. Jahan yeh line axis ko chhooti hai, wahi \(x\) ki value parhiye.
Yaad rakhiye: graph jitna saaf aur bara hoga, jawab utna hi theek parha jayega.

Ab kitab ki pehli misaal dekhte hain. Is mein interval diya hua hai, is liye humara kaam sirf graphs banana aur crossings parhna hai. Ghor kariye ke equation ke ek taraf sine hai aur doosri taraf seedhi line. Aisi equations ka koi seedha algebraic hal nahin, is liye yahi misaal graph wale tareeqe ki sab se achhi pehchaan hai.

blocks.title: Example 4
blocks.problem: Solve the equation \(\sin x = \frac{x}{2}\) graphically over the interval \([-\pi, \pi]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\sin x = \frac{x}{2}\), aur \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
Maloom karna: \([-\pi, \pi]\) mein \(x\) ki woh tamam values jo equation ko satisfy karti hain.
Tareeqa: sab se pehle hum dekhte hain ke equation mein \(\sin x\) aur \(\frac{x}{2}\) mile hue hain, is liye identity se kaam nahin chalega. Hum \(y = \sin x\) aur \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) ke graphs bana kar un ke milne ke points dhoondenge.

Step 1: Equation ko do functions mein todein
\[y = \sin x\]
\[y = \dfrac{x}{2}\]
Kyun: left side ek graph, right side doosra graph. Jis \(x\) par dono ki height barabar ho, wahan dono sides barabar hain, yani wahi solution hai.

Step 2: Values ki table
\(x = -\pi, -\frac{\pi}{2}, 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\) (yani taqreeban \(-3.14, -1.57, 0, 1.57, 3.14\)) par:
\(\sin x\): \(0, -1, 0, 1, 0\)
\(\frac{x}{2}\): \(-1.57, -0.79, 0, 0.79, 1.57\)
Kyun: \(y = \sin x\) jaani pehchaani lehar (wave) hai. \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) origin se guzarne wali seedhi line hai jis ka slope \(\frac{1}{2}\) hai; seedhi line ke liye do points kaafi hote hain.

Step 3: Dono graphs banaiye (Figure 10.1) aur crossings giniye
\(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par sine curve (1) line (0.79) se ooper hai; \(x = \pi\) par neeche hai (0 aur 1.57). Matlab \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan dono ek baar zaroor mile. Dono graphs origin se bhi guzarte hain. Aur left wala hissa right wale hisse ka aaina (mirror image) hai.
Kyun: \(\sin(-x) = -\sin x\) aur \(\frac{-x}{2} = -\frac{x}{2}\), yani dono odd functions hain. Is liye agar \(a\) root hai to \(-a\) bhi root hai. Aur roots nahin ho sakte: \(0 < x \le \frac{\pi}{2}\) par curve line se ooper hi rehti hai, aur \(|x| > 2\) par line ki height 1 se zyada ho jati hai jab ke \(\sin x\) kabhi 1 se aage nahin jata.
Dhyan dein: kisi bhi do points par "kaun ooper hai" ka badalna is baat ka saboot hai ke darmiyan mein crossing hui hai.

Step 4: Solutions parhiye
Graph (Figure 10.1) se nazar aata hai ke \([-\pi, \pi]\) mein curves teen points par milte hain. Is liye \(\sin x = \frac{x}{2}\) ke solutions yeh hain:
\[x = -1.89,\ 0 \text{ ya } 1.89 \text{ radians}\]
Kyun: solution crossing ka \(x\)-coordinate hai, us ki height (\(y\)) nahin. Bohat se students yahan \(0.95\) likh dete hain, jo ghalat hai.

Tasdeeq:
\[\sin(1.8955) \approx 0.9477\]
\[\dfrac{1.8955}{2} \approx 0.9477\]
Dono sides barabar aa gayin. Symmetry ki wajah se \(x = -1.8955\) bhi sahi hai, aur \(x = 0\) par \(0 = 0\). (Do decimal tak round karein to \(1.8955\) ka \(1.90\) banta hai; kitab ka \(1.89\) do decimal ke baad kaata hua (truncated) jawab hai, graph se parhi hui value ke liye yeh bhi qabil-e-qubool hai.)

blocks.alt: Graph on the interval minus pi to pi. The blue sine curve and the black straight line y = x/2 through the origin cross at three points: x about minus 1.90, x = 0 and x about 1.90. Dashed red lines drop from the two outer points to the x-axis.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.1: y = sin x and y = x/2 on [−π, π] (original drawing after the textbook's figure; the line is correctly labelled y = x/2)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ki Figure 10.1 mein seedhi line par "y = x" likha hai. Asal mein jo line bani hai (aur jo misaal mein use ho rahi hai) woh \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) hai: yeh point \(\left(\pi, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \approx (3.14, 1.57)\) se guzarti hai. Line \(y = x\) to \(y = \sin x\) ko sirf origin par milti, kyun ke \(x \ne 0\) ke liye hamesha \(|\sin x| < |x|\). Humari figure mein line par sahi label \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) laga hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Kitab ka Note: exact values numerical methods se aur behtar ki ja sakti hain, lekin graphical tareeqa ek saaf, nazar aane wala andaza (approximation) deta hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Graph se aam tor par ek ya do decimal tak hi sahi jawab milta hai. Jawab ko behtar karne ka aasan tareeqa "sign test" hai: \(\sin x - \frac{x}{2}\) ki value do qareebi points par nikaaliye. Agar ek par positive aur doosre par negative ho, to root un dono ke darmiyan hai.
Misal: \(x = 1.89\) par farq \(+0.0045\) hai aur \(x = 1.90\) par \(-0.0037\). Is liye root \(1.89\) aur \(1.90\) ke beech hai. Yeh kaam baar baar karein (har dafa faasla aadha) to root ki value aur aur theek hoti jati hai. Note mein jin numerical methods ka zikr hai, un ka bunyadi idea yahi hai.
Khud sochiye: \(x = 1.895\) par farq ka sign kya hoga? (Jawab: \(\sin 1.895 \approx 0.9479\) aur \(\frac{1.895}{2} = 0.9475\), farq positive, is liye root \(1.895\) aur \(1.90\) ke darmiyan hai.)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar equation \(\sin x = \frac{x}{4}\) hoti (line aur bhi dheemi charhti), to \([-\pi, \pi]\) mein kitne solutions hote, aur kahan?
Sochne ka tareeqa: line ab bhi origin se guzarti hai, aur dono functions ab bhi odd hain. \(x = \pi\) par line ki height \(\frac{\pi}{4} \approx 0.79\) hai jab ke \(\sin \pi = 0\); \(x = \frac{\pi}{2}\) par sine (1) line (0.39) se ooper hai. Yani \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan phir ek crossing hai.
Jawab: phir teen solutions, \(x = 0\) aur \(x \approx \pm 2.47\). Line jitni dheemi hogi, bahar wali crossings utni hi \(\pi\) ki taraf khisakti jayengi.
Agli misaal mein interval diya hi nahin gaya. Ab pehle humein khud tay karna hoga ke solutions kahan ho sakte hain. Yahan cosine ki range kaam aayegi.

blocks.title: Example 5
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\cos x = \frac{x}{8}\); koi interval nahin diya gaya.
Maloom karna: \(x\) ki tamam real values jo equation ko satisfy karti hain.
Tareeqa: \(y = \cos x\) aur \(y = \frac{x}{8}\) ke graphs ke milne ke points dhoondne hain. Lekin graph to poori number line par nahin bana sakte, is liye pehle cosine ki range se pata karenge ke solutions kis hisse mein ho sakte hain.

Step 1: \(\cos x\) ki range istemaal karein
\[-1 \le \cos x \le 1\]
\[\Rightarrow -1 \le \dfrac{x}{8} \le 1\]
\[\Rightarrow -8 \le x \le 8\]
Kyun: solution par \(\frac{x}{8}\) aur \(\cos x\) barabar hain, is liye \(\frac{x}{8}\) bhi \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hona chahiye. Teesri line mein hum ne poori inequality ko 8 se multiply kiya (8 positive hai, is liye signs nahin palte). \([-8, 8]\) se bahar line itni ooper ya neeche chali jati hai ke cosine ki lehar tak pohanch hi nahin sakti.

Step 2: \([-8, 8]\) par values ki table
\(x = -8, -6, -4, -2, 0, 2, 4, 6, 8\) par:
\(\cos x\): \(-0.15, 0.96, -0.65, -0.42, 1, -0.42, -0.65, 0.96, -0.15\)
\(\frac{x}{8}\): \(-1, -0.75, -0.5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1\)
Kyun: ab dono functions ko \([-8, 8]\) par plot karna hai. Line aahista aahista \((-8, -1)\) se \((8, 1)\) tak charhti hai, jab ke cosine ki lehar har \(2\pi \approx 6.28\) ke baad apne aap ko dohraati hai. (Cos ki values calculator ko radian mode mein rakh kar nikaliye.)

Step 3: Graph banaiye (Figure 10.2) aur crossings giniye
Lehar ke saath left se right chalte jaiye: line use paanch jagah kaatti hai, taqreeban \(-4.2\), \(-1.8\), \(1.4\), \(5.5\) aur \(6.8\) par.
Kyun: table ki dono rows ko milaiye; jahan "kaun bara hai" badal jaye, wahan graphs ek doosre ko cross kar chuke hote hain. \(x = 0\) par curve ki height \(1\) hai aur line ki \(0\); yahan dono alag alag hain, is liye origin par koi crossing nahin.
Dhyan dein: line origin se guzarti hai, magar cosine curve origin se nahin guzarti. Is liye \(x = 0\) ko solution samajhna ghalat hai.
Ek aur nukta: table mein \(x = 2\) aur \(x = 4\) ke darmiyan bhi dono values badalti hain, magar dono jagah cosine line se neeche hai (\(-0.42 < 0.25\) aur \(-0.65 < 0.5\)). Yahan "kaun ooper" nahin badla, is liye wahan koi crossing nahin. Sirf values ka badalna kaafi nahin; tarteeb ka badalna zaroori hai.

Step 4: Solutions parhiye
Graph (Figure 10.2) se nazar aata hai ke \([-8, 8]\) mein curves paanch points par milte hain. Is liye \(\cos x = \frac{x}{8}\) ke solutions taqreeban yeh hain:
\[x \approx -4.16,\ -1.80,\ 1.40\]
\[x \approx 5.46,\ 6.83\]
Kyun: yeh paanchon crossings ke \(x\)-coordinates hain. Kitab yahan chhe points, interval \([-\pi, \pi]\) aur \(x = 0\) likhti hai; yeh ghalat hai (neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye).

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 1.3955\): \(\cos x \approx 0.1744\) aur \(\frac{x}{8} \approx 0.1744\).
\(x = -4.1648\): \(\cos x \approx -0.5206\) aur \(\frac{x}{8} \approx -0.5206\).
Baaqi teen roots bhi isi tarah check hote hain: dono sides chaar decimal tak barabar aati hain. Aur \(x = 0\) par \(\cos 0 = 1 \ne 0\), yani \(0\) solution nahin.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 5 mein kitab "six points" likhti hai, solutions ko "in \([-\pi, \pi]\)" kehti hai, aur solutions ki list mein \(0\) bhi daal deti hai.
Sahi baat: curves sirf paanch points par milte hain, aur sab \([-8, 8]\) mein hain (jo interval Step 1 mein nikla). \(x = 0\) solution nahin, kyun ke \(\cos 0 = 1\) jab ke \(\frac{0}{8} = 0\); kitab ki apni Figure 10.2 bhi sirf paanch points dikhati hai.
Paanch roots do decimal tak: \(x \approx -4.16, -1.80, 1.40, 5.46, 6.83\) (zyada theek: \(-4.1648, -1.7974, 1.3955, 5.4643, 6.8307\)). Kitab ke \(1.39\) aur \(6.82\) round karne ke bajaye kaate hue hain.

blocks.alt: Graph on the interval minus 8 to 8. The blue cosine wave and the green straight line y = x/8 cross at five points, at x about minus 4.16, minus 1.80, 1.40, 5.46 and 6.83. The line passes through the origin, where the cosine curve is at height 1, so x = 0 is not a crossing.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.2: y = cos x and y = x/8 on [−8, 8] (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Is misaal se ek bari baat seekhne ko milti hai. Jab interval na diya ho, to graph banane se pehle yeh sochna zaroori hai ke solutions kis hisse mein reh sakte hain. Cosine aur sine kabhi \(-1\) se neeche ya \(1\) se ooper nahin jate, is liye jo doosri side hai (yahan \(\frac{x}{8}\)) use bhi isi pinjre (range) mein rehna parega. Isi se humein \([-8, 8]\) mila. Agar line \(\frac{x}{8}\) ke bajaye \(\frac{x}{20}\) hoti to interval \([-20, 20]\) banta aur crossings bhi zyada hotin, kyun ke lambe interval mein lehar zyada baar ooper neeche hoti hai. Aur ghor kijiye: figure mein \(x = 8\) ke qareeb line ki height 1 ke qareeb hai, magar cosine wahan neeche ja chuka hai, is liye kinaron par crossings khatam ho jati hain.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai, kitab ka sawal nahin: \(\cos x = x\) ke kitne solutions hain?
Range se: \(-1 \le x \le 1\). Is hisse mein \(y = x\) line \(-1\) se \(1\) tak charhti hai, aur \(\cos x\) \(0.54\) se \(1\) tak rehta hai, hamesha positive. Is liye negative \(x\) par koi crossing nahin. \(x = 0\) par curve ooper (1 aur 0), \(x = 1\) par line ooper (0.54 aur 1): darmiyan mein ek crossing.
Jawab: sirf ek solution, \(x \approx 0.739\). Tasdeeq: \(\cos(0.739) \approx 0.739\).
Ab ek aisi equation jis mein \(\tan x\) hai. Tan ka graph tukron (branches) mein hota hai, is liye yahan asymptotes ka khayal rakhna zaroori hai.

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem: Solve the equation \(\tan x = \frac{x}{2}\) graphically in \(\left[-\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\tan x = \frac{x}{2}\), \(x \in \left[-\frac{3\pi}{2}, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right]\).
Maloom karna: is interval mein \(x\) ki woh values jo equation ko satisfy karti hain.
Tareeqa: \(y = \tan x\) aur \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) ke milne ke points dhoondne hain. Yaad rakhiye ke \(\tan x\), \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke odd multiples par defined nahin, is liye us ka graph alag alag branches mein aata hai.

Step 1: Dono graphs ko pehchaaniye
\[y = \tan x, \qquad y = \dfrac{x}{2}\]
Interval mein \(\tan x\) ke vertical asymptotes: \(x = \pm\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(x = \pm\frac{3\pi}{2}\) (taqreeban \(\pm 1.57\), \(\pm 4.71\)).
Kyun: \(\tan x = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x}\), aur in points par \(\cos x = 0\), yani zero se divide. Asymptote (woh line jis ke qareeb graph jata hai magar use chhoota nahin) in jagahon par khari hoti hai. Do asymptotes ke darmiyan \(\tan x\) \(-\infty\) se \(+\infty\) tak charhta hai aur \(0, \pm\pi\) par zero se guzarta hai. Is tarah teen branches banti hain.

Step 2: Dono functions ko poore interval par plot karein (Figure 10.3)
Line \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) origin se guzarti hai, slope \(\frac{1}{2}\). \(x = \pm\frac{3\pi}{2}\) par bhi us ki height sirf \(\pm 2.36\) hai.
Kyun: seedhi line ke liye do points kaafi hain, maslan \((0, 0)\) aur \((4, 2)\).

Step 3: Har branch par alag alag crossings giniye
Darmiyani branch: dono graphs \((0, 0)\) se guzarte hain. \(0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2}\) par \(\tan x > x > \frac{x}{2}\), is liye yahan aur koi crossing nahin (symmetry se \(-\frac{\pi}{2} < x < 0\) par bhi nahin).
Right branch: \(\left(\frac{\pi}{2}, \pi\right)\) par \(\tan x\) negative hai aur \(\frac{x}{2}\) positive, is liye milna namumkin. \(\left(\pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}\right)\) par \(\tan x\) \(0\) se \(+\infty\) tak charhta hai jab ke line sirf \(1.57\) aur \(2.36\) ke beech hai: bilkul ek crossing.
Left branch: right branch ka aaina, is liye wahan bhi ek crossing.
Kyun: dono functions odd hain (\(\tan(-x) = -\tan x\)), is liye tasveer ka left hissa right hisse ko origin ke gird aadha chakkar ghuma kar milta hai.

Step 4: Solutions parhiye
Graph (Figure 10.3) se nazar aata hai ke interval mein curves teen points par milte hain. Is liye solutions taqreeban yeh hain:
\[x = -4.27,\ 0 \text{ aur } 4.27 \text{ radians}\]
Kyun: yeh teen crossings ke \(x\)-coordinates hain.

Tasdeeq:
\[\tan(4.2748) \approx 2.1374\]
\[\dfrac{4.2748}{2} = 2.1374\]
Dono sides barabar. Symmetry se \(x = -4.2748\) bhi sahi hai, aur \(\tan 0 = 0 = \frac{0}{2}\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab yahan "see figure 3" likhti hai; sahi hawala "Figure 10.3" hai.

blocks.alt: Graph on the interval minus 3 pi by 2 to 3 pi by 2. Three blue branches of y = tan x separated by dashed vertical asymptotes at minus 3 pi by 2, minus pi by 2, pi by 2 and 3 pi by 2. The black line y = x/2 crosses the left branch at about minus 4.27, the middle branch at the origin and the right branch at about 4.27.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.3: y = tan x and y = x/2 on [−3π/2, 3π/2] (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Interval ke kinare \(\pm\frac{3\pi}{2}\) khud asymptotes hain, jahan \(\tan x\) defined hi nahin; yeh kabhi solution nahin ban sakte.
Jab bhi \(\tan x\) ka graph banayein, pehle asymptotes ko dashed lines se draw karein, phir un ke darmiyan branches. Branch ko asymptote ke aar paar kabhi na jorein.
Khud sochiye: agar interval \(\left[-\frac{5\pi}{2}, \frac{5\pi}{2}\right]\) hota to kitne solutions hote? (Har nayi branch \(\left(2\pi, \frac{5\pi}{2}\right)\) mein ek crossing deti hai, aur us ka aaina bhi; is liye 5.)

Tan ke graph ke baare mein ek aur baat zehan mein rakhiye. Sine aur cosine ka period \(2\pi\) hai, magar tan ka period sirf \(\pi\) hai. Is ka matlab yeh hai ke tan ki har branch bilkul ek jaisi shakal ki hoti hai aur har \(\pi\) ke baad dohraai jati hai. Lekin is misaal mein doosri side \(\frac{x}{2}\) periodic nahin, woh har jagah alag height par hai. Is liye hum yeh nahin keh sakte ke "ek root mil gaya to \(\pi\) jor kar agla root mil jayega". Har branch ko alag se dekhna parta hai, jaisa Step 3 mein kiya. Periodicity wala shortcut sirf tab chalta hai jab dono sides periodic hon, jaise Example 7 mein. Yeh farq samajhna bohat zaroori hai, kyun ke students aksar \(4.27 + \pi\) ko bhi root likh dete hain, jo is interval se bahar bhi hai aur equation ko satisfy bhi nahin karta: \(x = 7.42\) par line ki height \(3.71\) hai jab ke \(\tan 7.42 \approx 2.14\).
Agli misaal mein dono taraf trigonometric functions hain, magar mukhtalif heights aur shift ke saath. Pehle har curve ki shakal samajhna aadha kaam hai.

blocks.title: Example 7
blocks.problem: Solve the equation \(3\cos x = 2\sin x - 1\) graphically in \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(3\cos x = 2\sin x - 1\), \(x \in [-2\pi, 2\pi]\).
Maloom karna: \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) mein \(x\) ki woh values jo equation ko satisfy karti hain.
Tareeqa: \(y = 3\cos x\) aur \(y = 2\sin x - 1\) ke graphs bana kar un ke milne ke points parhne hain.

Step 1: Dono curves ki shakal
\(y = 3\cos x\): cosine ki lehar jo 3 tak khinch gayi hai, yani \(-3\) aur \(3\) ke darmiyan.
\(y = 2\sin x - 1\): 2 height wali sine lehar jo 1 neeche khisak gayi hai, yani \(-3\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan.
Kyun: aage likha number lehar ko vertically khenchta hai (amplitude), aur \(-1\) poori lehar ko 1 unit neeche le jata hai.

Step 2: Values ki table
\(x = -2\pi, -\frac{3\pi}{2}, -\pi, -\frac{\pi}{2}, 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\) par:
\(3\cos x\): \(3, 0, -3, 0, 3, 0, -3, 0, 3\)
\(2\sin x - 1\): \(-1, 1, -1, -3, -1, 1, -1, -3, -1\)
Kyun: \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke multiples par sine aur cosine sirf \(0\) ya \(\pm 1\) hote hain, is liye values aasan hain aur dono lehrein banane ke liye kaafi hain.

Step 3: \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) par plot (Figure 10.4) aur ginti
Table se: \(-2\pi\) aur \(-\frac{3\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan, \(-\pi\) aur \(-\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan, \(0\) aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan, aur \(\pi\) aur \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan "kaun ooper" badalta hai. Yani chaar crossings.
Kyun: dono curves ka period \(2\pi\) hai. Jo do crossings \([0, 2\pi]\) mein hain, wahi \(2\pi\) peeche khisak kar \([-2\pi, 0]\) mein dobara aati hain.

Step 4: Solutions parhiye
Graph (Figure 10.4) se curves chaar points par milte hain. Is liye solutions taqreeban:
\[x \approx -5.02,\ -2.44\]
\[x \approx 1.26,\ 3.84\]
Kyun: dekhiye \(1.26 - 2\pi \approx -5.02\) aur \(3.84 - 2\pi \approx -2.44\); har root ka ek saathi \(2\pi\) baayein taraf hai. Kitab doosre root ko \(-2.43\) likhti hai; sahi \(-2.44\) hai (neeche dekhiye).

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 1.2638\): \(3\cos x \approx 0.9065\) aur \(2\sin x - 1 \approx 0.9065\).
\(x = 3.8434\): \(3\cos x \approx -2.2911\) aur \(2\sin x - 1 \approx -2.2911\).
Exact tasdeeq (hamari taraf se): \(3\cos x - 2\sin x = \sqrt{13}\cos(x + \alpha)\), jahan \(\alpha = \tan^{-1}\frac{2}{3}\). Equation ban jati hai \(\cos(x + \alpha) = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{13}}\), jis se bilkul yahi chaar roots nikalte hain: \(-5.0194, -2.4398, 1.2638, 3.8434\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab doosra root \(-2.43\) likhti hai. Asal root \(x = -2.4398\ldots\) hai, jo do decimal tak \(-2.44\) banta hai (yeh \(3.8434 - 2\pi\) hai). Baaqi teen values durust hain.

blocks.alt: Graph on the interval minus 2 pi to 2 pi. The blue curve y = 3 cos x (between minus 3 and 3) and the green curve y = 2 sin x minus 1 (between minus 3 and 1) cross at four points: x about minus 5.02, minus 2.44, 1.26 and 3.84.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.4: y = 3cos x and y = 2sin x − 1 on [−2π, 2π] (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Agar isi equation ka interval sirf \([0, 2\pi]\) hota to kitne solutions hote?
Sochne ka tareeqa: period \(2\pi\) hai, is liye ek poore chakkar mein crossings ka ek hi joda aata hai.
Jawab: do solutions, \(x \approx 1.26\) aur \(x \approx 3.84\). Interval \([-2\pi, 2\pi]\) do poore chakkar hai, is liye wahan chaar the.
Yeh periodicity ka faida hai: ek chakkar ke roots maloom hon to baaqi roots sirf \(2\pi\) jor ya ghata kar mil jate hain, naya graph banane ki zaroorat nahin.
Aakhri misaal mein ek curve square wali hai. Yeh misaal is liye bhi khaas hai ke ise exact tareeqe se bhi hal kiya ja sakta hai, aur hum dono jawabon ka muqabla karenge.

blocks.title: Example 8
blocks.problem: Solve the equation \(2\sin^2 x = 1 - 3\cos x\) graphically in \([0, 2\pi]\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(2\sin^2 x = 1 - 3\cos x\), \(x \in [0, 2\pi]\).
Maloom karna: \([0, 2\pi]\) mein \(x\) ki woh values jo equation ko satisfy karti hain.
Tareeqa: \(y = 2\sin^2 x\) aur \(y = 1 - 3\cos x\) ke milne ke points graph se dhoondne hain.

Step 1: Dono curves ki shakal
\(y = 2\sin^2 x\) kabhi negative nahin hota; \(0, \pi, 2\pi\) par \(0\) hai aur \(\frac{\pi}{2}\), \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) par sab se ooncha, yani \(2\).
\(y = 1 - 3\cos x\), \(x = 0\) par \(-2\) se shuru hota hai, \(x = \pi\) par \(4\) tak charhta hai, aur \(2\pi\) par wapas \(-2\).
Kyun: \(\sin^2 x\) hamesha \(0\) aur \(1\) ke darmiyan hai (square kabhi negative nahin). \(-3\cos x\) \(-3\) aur \(3\) ke darmiyan hai, aur \(1\) jorne se range \(-2\) se \(4\) ho jati hai.

Step 2: Values ki table
\(x = 0, \frac{\pi}{2}, \pi, \frac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\) par:
\(2\sin^2 x\): \(0, 2, 0, 2, 0\)
\(1 - 3\cos x\): \(-2, 1, 4, 1, -2\)
Kyun: in aasan points se pata chalta hai ke kis jagah kaun si curve ooper hai.

Step 3: \([0, 2\pi]\) par plot (Figure 10.5) aur ginti
\(\frac{\pi}{2}\) par green curve \(2\sin^2 x\) ooper hai (2 aur 1), \(\pi\) par blue curve \(1 - 3\cos x\) ooper hai (4 aur 0), aur \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) par phir green ooper. Is liye ek crossing \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) aur \(\pi\) ke darmiyan, aur ek \(\pi\) aur \(\frac{3\pi}{2}\) ke darmiyan. \(\left[0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) aur \(\left[\frac{3\pi}{2}, 2\pi\right]\) par blue curve green se neeche hi rehti hai.
Kyun: "kaun ooper" ka badalna batata hai ke darmiyan mein curves ne ek doosre ko kaata. Total sirf do crossings.

Step 4: Solutions parhiye
Graph (Figure 10.5) se curves \([0, 2\pi]\) mein do points par milte hain. Is liye solutions taqreeban:
\[x \approx 1.855 \text{ aur } 4.428 \text{ radians}\]
Kyun: yeh dono crossings ke \(x\)-coordinates hain. Kitab "four points" likhti hai magar khud bhi sirf do solutions deti hai; neeche ghalti ka box dekhiye.

Exact tasdeeq (hamari taraf se)
Identity \(\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x\) lagaiye:
\[2 - 2\cos^2 x = 1 - 3\cos x\]
\[2\cos^2 x - 3\cos x - 1 = 0\]
\[\cos x = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{17}}{4}\]
\(\frac{3 + \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx 1.78\) namumkin hai (cos kabhi 1 se zyada nahin), is liye \(\cos x = \frac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx -0.2808\):
\[x = \cos^{-1}(-0.2808) \approx 1.8554\]
\[x = 2\pi - 1.8554 \approx 4.4278\]
Kyun: yeh equation \(\cos x\) mein quadratic ban jati hai, is liye exact bhi hal ho sakti hai. Cosine negative hai, to angle quadrant II ya III mein hoga; \([0, 2\pi]\) mein aise sirf do angles hain. Graph ka jawab confirm ho gaya.
Dhyan dein: quadratic formula mein \(a = 2\), \(b = -3\), \(c = -1\); \(b^2 - 4ac = 9 + 8 = 17\).

Tasdeeq:
\(x = 1.8554\): \(2\sin^2 x \approx 1.8423\) aur \(1 - 3\cos x \approx 1.8423\).
\(x = 4.4278\) par bhi yahi values aati hain, kyun ke \(x\) ki jagah \(2\pi - x\) rakhne se na \(\sin^2 x\) badalta hai na \(\cos x\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 8 mein kitab "see figure 5", "the curves intersect at four points" aur root \(4.427\) likhti hai.
Sahi baat: hawala Figure 10.5 ka hai; curves \([0, 2\pi]\) mein sirf do points par milte hain (kitab ki apni figure aur do solutions ki list bhi yahi dikhati hai). Exact roots \(x = \cos^{-1}\frac{3 - \sqrt{17}}{4} \approx 1.855\) aur \(x = 2\pi - 1.855 \approx 4.428\) hain (4.4278 teen decimal tak 4.428 banta hai).

blocks.alt: Graph on the interval 0 to 2 pi. The blue curve y = 1 minus 3 cos x rises from minus 2 to 4 at pi and falls back to minus 2. The green curve y = 2 sin squared x has humps of height 2 at pi by 2 and 3 pi by 2. They cross at exactly two points, x about 1.86 and x about 4.43, both at height about 1.84.
blocks.caption: Figure 10.5: y = 2sin²x and y = 1 − 3cos x on [0, 2π] (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.text: Ab ek aham sawal: graph wala tareeqa kab use karein aur exact (algebraic) tareeqa kab? Agar equation ko identities ki madad se kisi ek trigonometric function, maslan sirf \(\cos x\) ya sirf \(\sin x\), ki equation bana sakte hain (jaise Example 8 mein \(\cos x\) ki quadratic bani), to exact tareeqa behtar hai, kyun ke us se bilkul durust jawab milta hai. Lekin agar equation mein \(x\) trigonometric function ke andar bhi ho aur bahar bhi (jaise Examples 4, 5 aur 6 mein), to exact tareeqa kaam nahin karta; wahan graph hi sahara hai. Aur jab sawal khud kahe "solve graphically", to graph banana hi zaroori hai, chahe exact tareeqa bhi mumkin ho. Aise mein exact jawab sirf apni tasdeeq ke liye istemaal kijiye.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text:
Exam mein "solve graphically" wale sawal ka jawab is tarteeb se likhiye:
1. Equation ko \(y = f(x)\) aur \(y = g(x)\) mein todiye aur likhiye ke kaun sa graph kis cheez ka hai.
2. Interval likhiye (ya range se nikaaliye, jaise Example 5 mein).
3. Dono functions ki values ki table dijiye.
4. Saaf graph banaiye, curves par naam likhiye (label), aur scale bataiye.
5. Crossings par dot laga kar \(x\)-axis tak dotted lines giraiye.
6. Aakhir mein saaf likhiye: "curves itne points par milte hain, is liye solutions yeh hain", aur jawab ke saath "radians" likhna mat bhooliye.
Examiner sab se pehle table, labels aur crossing points dekhta hai; in ke number aksar alag se milte hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(f(x) = g(x)\) ko graph se hal karne ke liye \(y = f(x)\) aur \(y = g(x)\) ek hi axes par banaiye; crossings ke \(x\)-coordinates solutions hain.
2. Jab \(x\) trigonometric function ke bahar bhi ho, to hamesha radians istemaal karein.
3. Interval na diya ho to trigonometric side ki range (maslan \(-1 \le \cos x \le 1\)) se solutions ka ilaqa tay karein.
4. \(\frac{\pi}{2}\) ke multiples par values ki table banaiye; jahan "kaun ooper" badle, wahan ek crossing hai.
5. Odd functions ki symmetry aur period (\(2\pi\), tan ke liye \(\pi\)) se baaqi roots jaldi mil jate hain.
6. Graph ka jawab andaza hai; har value ko dono sides mein rakh kar zaroor check karein.
7. Jahan equation kisi ek trigonometric function ki quadratic ban jaye (jaise Example 8), wahan exact jawab se graph ko confirm kar sakte hain.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Crossing ki height (\(y\)) ko jawab likh dena: solution hamesha \(x\)-value hai.
2. Aisa point jis se sirf ek graph guzarta ho (jaise Example 5 mein \(x = 0\)) ko solution maan lena. Bachne ka tareeqa: har jawab ko substitute kar ke dekhiye.
3. \(y = \frac{x}{2}\) jaisi line ke saath \(x\) ko degrees mein plot karna: scale radians ka hona chahiye.
4. \(\tan x\) ki branches ko asymptote ke aar paar jor dena.
5. Dono graphs ke liye alag alag scale lena, jis se crossings apni jagah se hat jati hain.
6. Calculator ko degree mode mein rakh kar \(\cos 2\) jaisi values nikaalna; yahan radian mode chahiye.
